title: Fragmented response assembly playbook (streaming + resume)
content:
Goal:
- Sketch a robust, minimal API and runtime choreography for assembling fragmented streaming responses across unstable networks, retries, and session-resume/offload.
- Primary use-case: client receives many small chunks (partial tokens / tool outputs / function-calls) and must rehydrate a coherent final response after reconnects or fetches from offload.

Constraints & assumptions:
- We must respect per-tenant size/latency SLOs.
- Backend can persist small checkpoints (KV blobs) keyed per session or request.
- Clients may be dumb (mobile) or smart (browser/edge). Provide simple canonical flows + optional enhancements.
- Should interoperate with Redwood prefix cache + KV-cache semantics.

High-level approach (playbook):
1) Emit stream fragments with explicit ids and relative ordering metadata.
2) Persist lightweight assembly manifests (append-only index) server-side at configurable thresholds.
3) Provide a compact resume API that returns missing fragments or a stitched snapshot.
4) Offer client-side heuristics for progressive replay, de-duplication, and fast-path display.

Key concepts / terms (informal):
- fragment: smallest transport unit we rely on (may be token, delta, tool output chunk).
- fragment-id: stable id for a fragment (uuid or monotonic-with-session).
- assembly-manifest: server-side index mapping sequence positions -> fragment ids + metadata.
- checkpoint: persisted snapshot (optionally compressed) that represents assembled state at a boundary.
- resume-token: stable short token issued by server describing resume state (opaque to client except for TTL).

API shapes (sketches) - prefer tiny, backwards-compatible additions:

1) Streaming response frame (transport-level envelope):
{
  "frame_type": "fragment",          // fragment | control | checkpoint
  "session_id": "s_abc123",
  "fragment_id": "f_0000001",
  "seq": 42,                         // monotonic integer within session/request
  "parent_seq": null,                // optional (for forks/call branches)
  "payload_type": "tokens",        // tokens | json-tool | binary-chunk
  "payload": "...base64 or utf8...",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-14T21:03:12Z",
  "partial_hash": "sha256:...",    // cheap integrity check
}

Notes: keep frame tiny; prefer utf8 payload for text tokens, base64 for binary. For function/tool outputs use payload_type json-tool and normalized JSON string.

2) Checkpoint frame (server-initiated):
{
  "frame_type": "checkpoint",
  "session_id": "s_abc123",
  "checkpoint_id": "cp_20260214_0001",
  "seq_up_to": 120,                  // includes fragments 1..120
  "manifest_blob_ref": "kv://sessions/s_abc123/cp_0001/manifest",
  "assembly_state_ref": "kv://sessions/s_abc123/cp_0001/state", // optional base64 compressed
  "resume_token": "rt:eyJzIjo...",   // opaque, short TTL
  "timestamp": "2026-02-14T21:05:00Z"
}

3) Resume API (client fetch) - HTTP/REST small JSON: POST /v1/sessions/:session_id/resume
Request:
{
  "client_resume_token": "rt:eyJzIjo...",   // optional, previously handed to client
  "want_from_seq": 1,                         // minimal seq client needs (optimistic)
  "max_bytes": 1_048_576                     // clamp response size
}

Response (happy):
{
  "resume_status": "stitchable",          // stitchable | partial | full-snapshot | missing
  "resolved_from_seq": 1,
  "fragments": [                             // order is canonical
    {"fragment_id":"f_0000001","seq":1,"payload_type":"tokens","payload":"Hello "},
    {"fragment_id":"f_0000002","seq":2,"payload_type":"tokens","payload":"world"}
  ],
  "checkpoint": {"checkpoint_id":"cp_0001","seq_up_to":120},
  "resume_token": "rt:eyJzIjo...",         // new token with renewed ttl
  "more_available": false
}

If resume_status=full-snapshot, server returns a single snapshot blob and optionally a small manifest describing how to validate.

Design choices and rationale:
- Use monotonic seq numbers per session to simplify ordering and idempotency.
- fragment_id must be stable and content-addressable preferred (sha256-of-payload + seq). Helps dedupe across retries.
- Keep resume-token opaque so we can evolve server-side state without coupling protocol.
- Checkpoints are asynchronously written; streaming continues after checkpoint commit. Client can request latest checkpoint reference when reconnecting.

Fragments vs checkpoint tradeoffs:
- Many small fragments: great for ultra-low-latency UX but expensive to rehydrate on resume (many small reads).
- Fewer larger checkpoints: cheaper resume, slower progressive UI.
- Provide server-configurable thresholds: fragment_count_threshold, bytes_threshold, time_window_seconds.

Server-side assembly sketch (append-only manifest):
- Each session has manifest chunk(s): list of records [seq, fragment_id, payload_ref, partial_hash, timestamp, payload_type].
- Manifest is append-only; compaction merges older fragments into checkpoint blobs (garbage collects manifest entries once checkpointed).

Compact manifest example (line oriented):
seq|fragment_id|payload_ref|hash|type|ts
1|f_0000001|kv://s/s_abc123/f_1|sha256:abcd|tokens|2026-02-14T21:03:12Z
2|f_0000002|kv://s/s_abc123/f_2|sha256:ef01|tokens|2026-02-14T21:03:12Z

Resume algorithm (server side):
- If resume_token provided: validate and load corresponding checkpoint/manifest offset.
- If want_from_seq > checkpoint.seq_up_to then return fragments from manifest for seq >= want_from_seq up to max_bytes.
- If too many fragments or too large, respond resume_status=partial and include a recommended checkpoint id to fetch (or server proactively return a snapshot).

Client heuristics (recommended):
- Maintain last_seq_received locally. On reconnect, call resume with want_from_seq=last_seq_received+1.
- If resume_status=stitchable: append returned fragments in order; verify partial_hash.
- If resume_status=full-snapshot: replace local display state with snapshot; optionally re-render differences for delta animation.
- De-dup: track fragment_ids for short TTL to avoid double-appending on occasional duplicate delivery.

Edge cases and notes:
- Branching (tool calls that produce parallel streams): include parent_seq to allow weaving two branches deterministically. Use (parent_seq, local_branch_id, seq) tuple for ordering if needed.
- Reordering during transport: sequence numbers + fragment_id enable reassembly out-of-order.
- Retention/GC: manifest lines older than last persisted checkpoint can be GC'd after safe TTL.
- Integrity: partial_hash on frames, checkpoint-level strong hash (sha256) on snapshot.

Operational knobs (config sketch):
- fragment_emit_interval_ms: 20 (default) -- how often to flush token buffer as a fragment.
- fragment_bytes_threshold: 4096 -- if a fragment grows larger cut a new one.
- checkpoint_interval_secs: 30 -- soft boundary for creating a snapshot.
- fragment_count_threshold_for_checkpoint: 128 -- force checkpoint if manifest grows too many entries.
- resume_max_response_bytes: 1_048_576 -- bound server responses.

Telemetry (what to emit):
- fragments_emitted_count, avg_fragment_size_bytes, resume_call_count, resume_success_rate, resume_latency_ms, checkpoint_write_latency_ms, fragments_per_resume_avg.

Sample flow (ASCII):
Client connects -> server streams frames:
[fragment:1] [fragment:2] [fragment:3] [checkpoint cp_1 seq_up_to=3] [fragment:4] ...
Client disconnects at seq=4. Reconnect: client sends resume want_from_seq=3 -> server returns fragments 3..6 or checkpoint snapshot depending on compaction.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we expose human-readable manifest endpoints for debugging? (yes but gated to admin scopes)
- Should we allow client-provided fragment_id to reduce server work? tradeoffs around malicious clients and dedupe.
- How to sign resume_token for cross-region resume without central KMS hops? consider compact signed JWT with region hint.
- UX: how to surface partial-snapshot for progressive display vs full-snapshot? add client-display-hints in frames.
- Backfill for historical sessions (billing/forensics): provide admin-only bulk export.

Compatibility notes:
- Make all new fields optional. Old clients that only expect plain streaming tokens should ignore unknown keys.
- Avoid large server-side syncs on every fragment (asynchronous checkpoint/manifest writes).

Stretch ideas (later):
- Delta-stream frames: payload can be "ops" that are client-display-aware (insert, delete) to enable animated reassembly.
- Hybrid: use a short-lived multicast push+KV-pull for clients behind flaky networks (push small resume_token then client pulls manifest).

Quick implementation plan (bootstrap):
- Phase 0: implement streaming frame envelope (server side) + client SDK decode/append logic.
- Phase 1: server manifest append + simple resume endpoint returning fragments array.
- Phase 2: checkpointing and resume_token with TTL + compaction/GC.
- Phase 3: admin debugging endpoints, metrics, cross-region resume optimizations.

Notes to self:
- Keep example API payloads minimal in the first iteration; avoid full payload dedupe complexity until we see real workload.
- Sync with UX/FE team about progressive display priorities (they prefer more frequent small fragments).
- Add grooming ticket to GH/INF once basic PoC works.

--- end of scratchpad ---
